page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is configured with 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes 236 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, while offering no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded capabilities, with gzip compression reaching 36.23 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.92 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 4655.9 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 29.51 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is average, with read-only small block cached speeds at 345.13 GB/sec, though large block write speeds are weaker at 23.53 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a dense compute profile with a low memory footprint, making it suitable for workloads that require high clock speeds but do not demand large memory capacities. The inclusion of 236 GB of local storage provides a resource-dense option for temporary data handling. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic database operations, but is less optimal for memory-intensive applications or heavy multi-threaded workloads like large-scale LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features a low 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and includes 236 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities. The processor features a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance, particularly in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression tasks, though multi-core execution and write-heavy memory operations are comparatively weak. This configuration provides a qualitatively cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring high CPU clock speeds without massive memory overhead. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded processing, and basic database operations.
